identity_policy.version_rule: Keep the identity for the same observable construct; store a separate integer version. Materially different outcomes receive a new ID, with a documented migration rather than silent reuse.
identity_policy.namespace_note: These are proposed documentation-level concept identities. No runtime schema, lesson IDs or event storage are changed by this deliverable.

coverage_status_meanings.existing_material: Identifiable existing explanation or activity content addresses the proposed construct. This does not mean accurate, sufficient, accessible or assessed.
coverage_status_meanings.partial: Some relevant material exists, but the stated prerequisite/outcome or its application/check needs explicit additional authoring.
coverage_status_meanings.missing: No dedicated introductory material and prerequisite check for this construct were found in the inspected course. Any linked lesson is an assumption context, not proof of coverage.

dependency_policy: prerequisite_ids lists proposed instructional prerequisites for the stated outcome. Edges are not learned-user state, enforced runtime locks or a claim that this is the only valid teaching order.

candidate_jobs.label: Refresh technical fundamentals for current work
candidate_jobs.trigger: A person needs to discuss or choose an algorithm or structure in an actual work decision after time away from the topic.
candidate_jobs.desired_observable_outcome: Explain a relevant tradeoff and apply it to a real bounded work example with stated assumptions.
candidate_jobs.evidence_needed: Recent work example, current workaround, recurrence and a feasible learning moment; later behavior and delayed/application observations.
candidate_jobs.exclusions: Does not presume interview pressure, a broad credential goal or willingness to pay.

candidate_jobs.label: Prepare for a technical interview
candidate_jobs.trigger: A person has an upcoming technical interview and needs to explain and implement relevant patterns.
candidate_jobs.desired_observable_outcome: Read a bounded problem, justify an approach, trace an edge case and implement a suitable solution under an explicitly chosen practice format.
candidate_jobs.evidence_needed: A recent interview-preparation attempt, target assessment format, knowledge gaps, time pressure and actual study or purchase behavior.
candidate_jobs.exclusions: Does not claim the course matches a particular employer assessment or guarantee hiring outcomes.

candidate_jobs.label: Understand algorithms out of curiosity
candidate_jobs.trigger: A person wants an intelligible explanation of a technical idea without a current work or interview deadline.
candidate_jobs.desired_observable_outcome: Explain one interesting idea in their own words and choose whether to explore a related example later.
candidate_jobs.evidence_needed: A recent voluntary learning episode, reasons to return or stop, acceptable effort and alternatives already used.
candidate_jobs.exclusions: Does not assume professional urgency, need for timed coding or the same payment rationale as the other jobs.

concepts.label: Program state and control flow
concepts.observable_outcome: Given a short assignment, conditional and loop, record the variable values after each step and state when the loop stops.
concepts.coverage_note: The course uses variables, functions, conditionals, references and loops throughout but has no dedicated introduction or prerequisite check for these basics. Linked lessons are contexts that assume this knowledge, not substitute prerequisite lessons.

questions: What minimum code-reading check distinguishes a learner who can trace assignments and branches from one who needs an introductory route?

concepts.label: Indices and interval boundaries
concepts.observable_outcome: For an array and inclusive low/high bounds, identify valid indices, the current candidate interval and the empty-interval condition.
concepts.coverage_note: Direct indexing and low/high are shown, but boundary conventions and empty-input checks are not taught or assessed systematically.

questions: Which boundary conventions, empty inputs and duplicate-value contracts must be stated before a trace is scored?

concepts.label: Sorted order and comparator meaning
concepts.observable_outcome: Given values and a comparator, identify whether they are in nondecreasing order and justify which values can be excluded by a comparison.
concepts.coverage_note: Sorted/nondecreasing input is stated as a requirement in search and merge material, but no standalone prerequisite explanation and check establish this knowledge.

questions: How will an author establish ordering, equality and the comparator contract before using safe elimination or merging?

concepts.label: Recursion state and base cases
concepts.observable_outcome: Trace a small recursive call tree, name each call state and show how a base case and decreasing subproblem prevent further calls.
concepts.coverage_note: Recursive examples and base cases are present, but there is no dedicated introductory recursion lesson or prerequisite assessment; the learning-home recursion module is only a catalogue item.

questions: Which call-stack and termination foundations need an authored bridge before recursive sorting, traversal and memoization?

concepts.label: Input size, operation model and cases
concepts.observable_outcome: For a stated implementation, name the input-size variable, counted operation, case being discussed and whether extra copies or call-stack space are included.
concepts.coverage_note: Growth and tradeoffs are introduced, but the cost model, average-case assumptions and memory-accounting conventions are not consistently explicit.

questions: Can learners distinguish an algorithm family, the shown implementation, an average-case assumption and an auxiliary-space convention?

concepts.label: Halving and logarithmic decisions
concepts.observable_outcome: For candidate sets of 8 and 32 items, count successive halvings to a singleton and explain why doubling the size adds one halving step in this example.
concepts.coverage_note: Halving and logarithmic growth are described, but the mathematical bridge and its limits need a specific checked example.

questions: What numerical example explains the logarithmic claim without requiring unintroduced logarithm notation?

concepts.label: Tree vocabulary and height
concepts.observable_outcome: On a labelled rooted tree, identify root, child, subtree and leaf, and compute the stated edge-count height convention.
concepts.coverage_note: Nodes and children appear in BST explanations, while root/subtree/height are used across lessons without a dedicated vocabulary and convention check.

questions: Which height convention and empty-tree treatment will the content use consistently?

concepts.label: Graph edges, direction and weight
concepts.observable_outcome: Given a small graph, list vertices and edges, state whether edges are directed and compare hop count with the sum of edge weights.
concepts.coverage_note: Lists, matrices and weighted paths are described, but foundational graph assumptions differ across examples and need explicit checks.

questions: Do examples state directedness, unreachable vertices, edge weights and whether every vertex appears in the representation?

concepts.label: Map and set operation contracts
concepts.observable_outcome: Trace insert, membership lookup and value retrieval on a small map or set, keeping key identity distinct from the stored value.
concepts.coverage_note: Map and Set APIs are used in code and hash buckets are discussed, but an introductory API/identity contract and prerequisite check are absent.

questions: What is assumed about equality, key/value access and average lookup cost before maps and visited sets are used?

concepts.label: Prefixes and subsequences
concepts.observable_outcome: For two short strings, distinguish a prefix by length, a contiguous substring and an order-preserving subsequence using explicit character positions.
concepts.coverage_note: LCS uses prefixes and subsequences without a dedicated explanation or check distinguishing them from substrings; the linked material is an assumption context.

questions: How will prefix length and half-open indexing be distinguished from inclusive endpoints before the LCS recurrence?

concepts.label: Stable ordering of equal keys
concepts.observable_outcome: Given records with equal sort keys and distinct identities, show whether a proposed sorted result preserves their original relative order.
concepts.coverage_note: Stability is asserted and used in choices, but no dedicated definition, equal-key example or prerequisite check is authored.

questions: Will a record-with-equal-keys example make stability observable rather than a memorized algorithm label?

concepts.label: A state property preserved by a loop

concepts.coverage_note: Many lessons name a local invariant, but the shared idea of initialization, preservation and a bounded conclusion is not taught as a prerequisite unit.

questions: What small worked proof establishes preservation and termination without assuming learners already understand the word invariant?

worked_activity_drafts.label: Explain a safe discard
worked_activity_drafts.prompt: In [3, 7, 11, 15, 19], the target is 19 and the midpoint value is 11. Which indices remain possible after comparison, and why can the others be discarded?
draft_rubric_criteria: Uses the stated zero-based inclusive convention: indices 3 through 4 remain.
Connects the discard to ordered values at or below 11, rather than simply saying move right.
Preserves the if-present candidate claim; does not claim the target has been found by this step.
worked_activity_drafts.evidence_rule: Private thinking remains unscored. A submitted answer requires an actual reviewed assessment outcome and an assistance record; this fixture creates no learner evidence.

worked_activity_drafts.label: Choose a search approach for a changing directory
worked_activity_drafts.prompt: A directory receives frequent additions and is queried both once during import and repeatedly during the day. What would you ask before choosing a linear scan or binary search, and under what conditions would each be reasonable?
draft_rubric_criteria: Asks whether a maintained order/comparator and the required access model exist.
Distinguishes one-off lookup from repeated queries and includes preprocessing or update-maintenance cost.
Gives a conditional choice and names missing facts instead of asserting that binary search is always faster.
worked_activity_drafts.evidence_rule: Private thinking remains unscored. A submitted answer requires an actual reviewed assessment outcome and an assistance record; this fixture creates no learner evidence.

worked_activity_drafts.label: Explain the next merged value
worked_activity_drafts.prompt: Merge [1, 4, 4] and [2, 4, 7] in nondecreasing order. After output [1, 2], what value can be emitted next, which cursor moves, and why is the remaining output still constructible?
draft_rubric_criteria: Chooses a smallest remaining front value 4 under a stated tie policy.
Advances only the consumed cursor and leaves the other candidates available.
Explains that each input remainder is already ordered and includes a plan to drain leftovers.
worked_activity_drafts.evidence_rule: Private thinking remains unscored. A submitted answer requires an actual reviewed assessment outcome and an assistance record; this fixture creates no learner evidence.

worked_activity_drafts.label: Merge two timestamped batches
worked_activity_drafts.prompt: Two event batches are individually ordered by timestamp. Equal timestamps must preserve their agreed original sequence across batches. State the extra ordering/tie information you need, then explain how a merge can preserve it.
draft_rubric_criteria: Requests a cross-batch original-order or tie-break contract; equal timestamps alone do not specify it.
Maintains the ordered output-prefix invariant and consumes one input record at a time.
Explains that left-first on equal keys is stable only when the input ordering and agreed tie contract support it.
worked_activity_drafts.evidence_rule: Private thinking remains unscored. A submitted answer requires an actual reviewed assessment outcome and an assistance record; this fixture creates no learner evidence.

limits: Every intended outcome, prerequisite edge and activity alignment is an assistant-authored candidate pending subject review; none is human educational approval.
All 41 source lessons and 205 source blocks are inventoried. This is coverage of the reviewed repository, not a claim to cover all algorithms or to offer a validated beginner curriculum.
Current multiple-choice checks test selected options. Existing lab/project declarations do not establish valid reasoning assessment, delayed recall or transfer.
Private recall stays unscored; audio/read completion is exposure. New prompt/rubric examples are drafts and create no learner observations.
Existing nine-minute lesson estimates and the source validator twelve-minute limit are authoring choices, not measured timing or universal microlearning optima.
This task does not select a cohort or expand the catalogue. BB-GTM-001 and BB-LRN-003 own cohort selection and the bounded reviewed pilot path.
